summary: The note describes the Marshall Plan, officially the European Recovery Program (ERP), an American initiative to give economic aid to Western Europe after World War II. It states the plan ran for four years from April 1948 and lists US goals of rebuilding war-torn regions, removing trade barriers, modernising industry, improving prosperity, and preventing the spread of Communism. The note contains two near-duplicate versions of the same paragraph that disagree on the aid total, the 2016/2017 dollar equivalents, the start date, and the spelling of 'modernise' versus 'modernize'.
one_line: The Marshall Plan (European Recovery Program), a 1948-era four-year American economic aid program to rebuild Western Europe after World War II.
key_facts: The Marshall Plan was officially called the European Recovery Program (ERP).
The Marshall Plan was an American initiative to aid Western Europe after the end of World War II.
One version of the note says the United States gave over $13 billion (nearly $140 billion in 2017 dollars) in economic assistance under the Marshall Plan.
The other version of the note says the United States gave over $12 billion (nearly $100 billion in 2016 US dollars) in economic assistance under the Marshall Plan.
One version says the Marshall Plan was in operation for four years beginning on April 8, 1948.
The other version says the Marshall Plan was in operation for four years beginning on April 3, 1948.
The stated goals of the United States were to rebuild war-torn regions, remove trade barriers, modernise industry, improve European prosperity, and prevent the spread of Communism.
The Marshall Plan required a lessening of interstate barriers and a dropping of many regulations.
The Marshall Plan encouraged an increase in productivity and trade union membership.
The Marshall Plan encouraged the adoption of modern business procedures.
The two versions of the note use 'modernise' and 'modernize' respectively for the goal of modernising industry.
The note's two paragraphs are near-duplicates, differing in the aid amount, dollar equivalents, and start date.
